Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 74, verses 1–7:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One), because it speaks of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) at the beginning of revelation and describes him as al-Muddaththir, that is, one who wraps himself in a garment or the like. This indicates the greatness of the matter of revelation and the sublimity of its status.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• The honouring of the Prophet (ﷺ) with the message, and his being charged with rising to bear the burdens of the call and carrying out the task of conveying it, and with patience over the harm of the wicked, and with proclaiming the Oneness of God, exalting Him, and rejecting polytheism (shirk).

• A warning to the criminals of a grievous and severe Day, and the presentation of the story of one of the polytheists who recognised the truth but abandoned it out of obstinacy, and who set himself to attack the Qur'an and claimed that it was the word of a human being.

• A description of Hell (Jahannam), which God has prepared for the disbelievers, by mention of its guardians, who are fierce, and its angels of punishment (zabaniyah), who have been charged with tormenting its inhabitants, and mention of the dialogue that takes place between the believers and the criminals about the cause of their entry into the Blazing Fire, and within it a clarification of the state of the opposite party, namely the believers.

[The Exegesis]

O you who have wrapped himself in his garments, arise from your resting-place, and warn the people of the punishment of God. Single out your Lord alone for glorification, Oneness and worship. Purify your garments from impurities, for the purity of the outward is part of the completeness of the purity of the inward. Persist in forsaking idols, images and all the acts of polytheism, so do not draw near to them. Do not give a gift seeking to receive more in return, and for the sake of the good pleasure of your Lord, be patient in obeying the commands and avoiding the prohibitions.

Leave me alone, O Messenger, with the one whom I created alone and unique in his mother's womb, and to whom I gave abundant wealth spread out, and sons present with him in Makkah who never leave him, and whom I made life easy for with ease. Then he hopes, after this bounty, that I will increase him in wealth and children. Indeed, he has disbelieved in Me. The matter is not as this wicked sinner claims. I will not increase him beyond that; indeed, he was stubborn and a denier toward the Qur'an and the proofs of Allah upon His creation. I will impose upon him a hardship of punishment and distress from which he will have no relief. The one meant by this threat is al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who opposed the truth and openly fought against Allah and His Messenger with hostility. And this is the recompense of everyone who opposes the truth and rejects it.

He reflected within himself and prepared what he would say to disparage Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an.

Then he was cursed, and deserved destruction. How he prepared this slander in his mind! Then he was cursed again. Then he reflected on what he had planned and prepared of slander against the Qur'an. Then he frowned and scowled and grew severe in his displeasure, because his schemes had run out and he found no way to slander the Qur'an. Then he turned away from the truth, and was too proud to acknowledge it. So he said about the Qur'an: "This is nothing but magic, transmitted from the ancients. This is nothing but the speech of created beings, which Muhammad learned from them," and then he claimed that it came from Allah.

I will cast him into Hell, so that he will endure its heat and be burned by its fire. And what will make you know what Hell is? It leaves no flesh and spares no bone without burning it. It changes the skin and blackens the hides, and it burns them. Over it are nineteen angels, the fierce guardians (az-Zabaniyah), who are in charge of its affairs and have power over its people to punish them.

And We have not made the guardians of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve in Allah; so that those who were given the Scripture, from the Jews and the Christians, may attain certainty that what the Qur'an says about the guardians of Hell is truly from Allah, since it agrees with their books; and the believers may increase in faith in Allah and His Messenger and in acting upon His law. Those who were given the Scripture, from the Jews and the Christians, and the believers in Allah and His Messenger, will not doubt this. And so that those in whose hearts is hypocrisy and the disbelievers will say: "What did Allah intend by this strange number?" Thus Allah leads astray whom He wills, and guides whom He wills. None knows the hosts of your Lord—among them the angels—except Allah alone. And it (the Fire) is nothing but a reminder and an admonition to mankind.

Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned of evil deeds and wrongdoing, and it will not be released until it has paid what it owes of rights and punishments, except the sincere Muslims, the companions of the right hand, who have freed their necks through obedience. They are in gardens whose description cannot be grasped. They will ask one another about the disbelievers who committed crimes against their own souls: ﴿What has brought you into Hellfire?﴾ and ﴿made you taste its blaze?﴾ The criminals will say: "We were not among those who prayed in the world, nor did we give charity or show kindness to the poor and the needy. We used to engage in vain talk with the people of misguidance and error, and we used to deny the Day of Reckoning and Recompense, until death came to us while we were in those errors and evil deeds."

We used to engage in vain talk with the people of misguidance and error, and we used to deny the Day of Reckoning and Recompense, until death came to us while we were in those errors and evil deeds."

Truly, the Qur'an is an eloquent admonition, sufficient for them to take heed. Whoever wishes to take heed will be admonished by what it contains and will benefit from its guidance. They will not take heed unless God wills guidance for them. He, glorified is He, is worthy of being feared and obeyed, and worthy of forgiving those who believe in Him and obey Him.
